rounds.text: Raasi Refractories is currently undergoing a significant operational turnaround that is not yet reflected in stale market sentiment [E58]. The company has demonstrated exceptional top-line momentum, achieving 60% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E16] and 34% year-over-year sales growth [E51]. This performance is supported by a strong sector tailwind in Capital Goods [E57, E59], which provides a favorable macro backdrop for the business to scale [E57]. Furthermore, the company is explicitly expected to deliver a good quarter [E44], suggesting that the recent acceleration in net profit [E58] is part of a sustainable trend. Conceded: [E15, E18, E19, E20, E24, E25, E29, E30, E31, E33, E45, E46, E47, E48, E49, E55, E56]. Despite the cautious market view, the company’s ability to generate strong sales growth [E52] and profit growth [E53, E54] positions it to outperform the current, overly pessimistic valuation [E58].

The valuation is fundamentally disconnected from reality, trading at a P/E of 31.1x [E1] and an elevated EV/EBITDA of 14.52x against a sector benchmark of 12.66x [E11], while a discounted cash flow model reveals a massive negative margin of safety of -190.3% [E39] with an intrinsic value of just Rs 6 per share [E38]. Operational health is deeply compromised, evidenced by negative operating cash flow of Rs -7.34 Cr and free cash flow of Rs -7.51 Cr in Mar 2026 [E30, E31], alongside a staggering debtor period of 224 days [E49] and rising borrowings of Rs 37.40 Cr [E33]. Furthermore, structural profitability is poor with a 5-year profit growth of -19% [E18] and a 3-year profit contraction of -48% [E19], while reported earnings are artificially propped up by Rs 3.92 Cr of other income [E48]. Extreme promoter risk hangs over the equity with 99.8% of promoter holdings pledged [E47], compounded by a low interest coverage ratio [E45] and contingent liabilities of Rs 3.90 Cr [E46]. Conceded: the company displays strong short-term sales growth of 60% over the trailing twelve months [E16] and operates within a capital goods sector tailwind [E57].

Conceded: the discounted cash flow model suggests a lower intrinsic value [E38] and operating cash flow was negative in Mar 2026 [E30]. However, the business is demonstrating explosive operational acceleration with a 60% compounded sales growth over the trailing twelve months [E16] alongside strong recent metrics including net profit up 46% year-on-year [E53]. Furthermore, the company benefits directly from a robust Capital Goods sector tailwind with a supportive tailwind score of +0.68 [E59] and is explicitly expected to deliver a good upcoming quarter [E44]. Sentiment and static models are lagging behind genuine accelerating business results, which score an impressive 98 out of 100 on recent performance [E58].

While the bull highlights recent sales growth, this performance is disconnected from the company’s underlying financial health, as evidenced by a 69% decline in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E20]. Conceded: the company is flagged for a potentially good upcoming quarter [E44]. However, this optimism is undermined by a severe lack of cash generation, with operating cash flow reaching Rs -7.34 Cr and free cash flow at Rs -7.51 Cr in March 2026 [E30, E31]. The bull’s reliance on recent growth metrics ignores the structural risk posed by the fact that 99.8% of promoter holdings are pledged [E47]. Furthermore, the company’s reliance on "other income" of Rs 3.92 Cr to bolster earnings [E48] and the presence of high debtors of 224 days [E49] suggest that the reported profit growth is not supported by high-quality operational cash inflows. Finally, the market is pricing in 12.6% earnings growth [E40] despite a three-year compounded profit growth rate of -48% [E19], indicating that the current valuation is built on speculative expectations rather than consistent delivery.
